page: Google Cloud Platform m3-ultramem-64 is an ultra-high-memory instance tailored for massive in-memory workloads. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz, this instance provisions 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache hierarchy comprises 48 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and a large 54 MB shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI, along with hardware cryptography acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI instructions.

The core characteristic of m3-ultramem-64 is its memory capacity of 1952.0 GB of RAM, yielding an extreme memory density of 30.5 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated hardware accelerators, meaning operating system and data volumes rely entirely on remote network-attached block storage, and all computation executes strictly on CPU cores. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 151.05 GB/sec, while uncached write bandwidth measures 61.86 GB/sec, supporting high-throughput memory streaming.

Benchmark testing reveals strong multi-threaded execution metrics, placing in the top 25 percent for PassMark CPU score (55325.27) and Geekbench multi-core score (16753.0). In particular, database operations in PassMark achieved a strong score of 26390.07, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieved 80.97 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core execution remains in the middle 50 percent, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1584.0 and stress-ng single-core result of 1844.58. The instance also achieved 53.89 million Redis SET operations per second and 42.63 GB/sec static web serving throughput.

From a resource allocation standpoint, m3-ultramem-64 represents a specialized hardware class where investment concentrates heavily into volatile system memory rather than raw compute cycles or local NVMe pools. As a result, deploying workloads with modest memory demands would be economically inefficient. The instance fits enterprise in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, massive distributed caching tiers, in-memory graph analytics, and large ETL data transformations requiring near-two-terabyte working sets resident in memory.
description: Google Cloud Platform m3-ultramem-64 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine engineered for substantial in-memory enterprise workloads. It is powered by a 2.6 GHz Intel Xeon processor providing 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading, supported by 54 MB of L3 cache, AVX-512, and cryptographic hardware extensions. The instance is defined by 1952.0 GB of system memory, providing an extensive 30.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. There is no bundled local storage or discrete GPU hardware, necessitating external network block storage for persistent data. In benchmark evaluations, m3-ultramem-64 displays strong multi-core compute capability, with top-tier results in PassMark database operations, Geekbench multi-core workloads, and software compilation, alongside an average single-core performance profile. Due to the substantial resource density leaning toward RAM, this instance delivers strong qualitative efficiency for memory-bound applications, including massive in-memory databases, large caching layers, high-scale ETL pipelines, and memory-intensive data analytics.
